sources.news_title: Man Shot & Killed On Subway Platform In New York City Following Argument
sources.text:
An argument on a subway platform in midtown Manhattan turned deadly Saturday (Oct. 17). The incident left one man fatally shot and disrupted train service. This comes just weeks after another man died at the Brooklyn subway station in September.
RELATED: Pregnant Woman Identified As 1 Of 8 Victims In Pennsylvania Shooting As Attacker’s Identity Is Revealed (UPDATE)
Details About The Shooting
The shooting happened around 12:20 p.m. at the station at 7th Avenue and 53rd Street. The location is a short walk from several Broadway theaters and Carnegie Hall. Police found an adult man with a gunshot wound to his chest. A police spokesperson said the shooting took place on the E train platform. The dispute involved two or three men. Trains that normally stop at that station were bypassing the area while a police investigation was underway. Emergency crews responded and transported the victim to Bellevue Hospital, where doctors pronounced him dead. No arrests were immediately reported.
Man Dragged At Another NYC Subway
Last month, a New York City subway train man dragged a man to death. The accident occurred during the Monday evening rush-hour commute on Sept. 28. Yaw Boahene, 57, was exiting the train at a Brooklyn subway station when his bag, which police described as a shopping bag, snagged in the closing train doors. The Brooklyn resident was pulled onto the tracks and run over by the train as it left the station, police said in a statement. Officers arrived to find Boahene “unconscious and unresponsive” on the train tracks, police said. He was pronounced dead at the scene.
Stay Connected
Subscribe to updates from The Shade Room
Dragging deaths happen from time to time on the nation’s largest subway system. In 2022, a 20-year-old commuter was killed, per ABC7. This happened after his backpack or a piece of his clothing got stuck in the door as he was trying to get onto a train at the Columbus Circle station in upper Manhattan.
Violence In New York City Reportedly Trending Downward
Violent crime has been dropping steadily in New York City since a spike during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. Also, deadly violence inside the subway system remains rare, despite the trains being used by millions of people each day. Through mid-October, the city was on pace to have its lowest number of killings in decades. Reported homicides were down 20% from the same point last year.
RELATED: Social Media Calls For Arrest Of Mother Of 16-Year-Old Oregon School Shooter For Allegedly Purchasing Weapon Used In Attack
Associated Press contributed to this report via AP Newsroom.

sources.news_title: Man, 34, fatally shot in chest in Midtown Manhattan subway station
NYPD: Man Fatally Shot Inside Midtown Manhattan Subway Station
sources.text:
A man was fatally shot inside a New York City subway station Saturday afternoon, police confirmed to News Outlet.
The shooting occurred shortly after noon at the 53rd Street and 7th Avenue station in busy Midtown Manhattan, according to the NYPD.
Hassen Pinchback, a visitor from Orlando, Florida, told News Outlet that he saw the aftermath and watched as passengers began running when the gunfire erupted.
“It was like a stampede,” he said.
Pinchback said the gunfire began when the train doors opened. “That’s when you heard pop pop pop,” he recalled. He added that a female bystander performed chest compressions on the victim before officers arrived, urging him to “Hang in there.”
Another witness from Washington state, who identified herself only by the last name Miller, said she and her daughter were inside a subway car with its doors open when they heard about five shots. Her daughter stepped outside, and the shooter looked directly at her before continuing to fire.
“I just started praying. I’m a very strong Christian,” she said. “Jesus saved us. 100%.”
MORE ON THIS: Mexico Jails 3 Men 158 Years Each for Killing US, Australian Surfers
Miller said her daughter signaled to the conductor of another train that a gunman was present. The conductor then called 911.
The victim was taken to a hospital in critical condition, where he later succumbed to his injuries.
Police said no arrests had been made and that the investigation remained ongoing, the NYPD told News Outlet.
PIX11 reported that the shooting followed an argument between the victim and the shooter.

sources.news_title: Man fatally shot during dispute at Midtown Manhattan subway station, police say
sources.text:
A man died Saturday after being shot during a dispute at a subway station in Manhattan’s Theater District, according to police.
Officers responded to reports of gunfire at the 53rd Street and Seventh Avenue subway station around 12:21 p.m., police said. The victim was taken to a nearby hospital, where he was pronounced dead at 1:06 p.m.
The station serves Midtown Manhattan, an area crowded with tourists and theatergoers.
Authorities did not name the victim, pending notification of his family, and said he was “possibly” in his 30s.
Police are searching for a man in connection with the shooting. In a statement, NYPD said the man approached the victim on the northbound E train platform, shot him once in the chest and fled on foot.
At a news conference, police said a dispute between two men moved from the platform onto a train and back onto the platform. Investigators were still determining where the shots were fired, police said at the briefing.

sources.news_title: Man killed in NYC subway station shooting, officials say
sources.text:
Man killed in NYC subway station shooting, officials say
A man was killed in a shooting at a Midtown Manhattan subway station Saturday, officials say.
It happened on the northbound E train platform at the Seventh Avenue station near West 53rd Street just before 12:30 p.m.
Police said two men got into a dispute on the platform. According to the NYPD, the dispute spilled onto a train that had pulled into the station, then back onto the platform.
It's unclear at this time if the shots were fired on the platform or on the train, police said in a press conference Saturday afternoon.
Authorities say the victim was shot in the chest and taken to a local hospital in critical condition, where he was pronounced dead. Police say they are not releasing the victim's identity until family has been notified, but the victim was possibly in his 30s.
Police say the gunman fled on foot. No arrests have been made. The NYPD has released photos of a person wanted in connection to the shooting. He was last seen wearing a red tracksuit, a black vest and a black face mask.
No weapons were recovered at the scene, police say.
Anyone with information is urged to call the NYPD's Crime Stoppers Hotline at 1-800-577-TIPS (8477), or for Spanish, 1-888-57-PISTA (74782). The public may also submit tips online at Crime Stoppers website or via X @NYPDTips.
The investigation is ongoing.
The MTA said they are coordinating with the NYPD and working to retrieve surveillance footage from cameras on the platform and train cars.
"Guns have no place in transit which is why we've strongly supported New York State's legal fight to make sure it's illegal to carry them in the subway system," Kemper said in a statement, in part. "The perpetrator will be caught and should face maximum consequences from the justice system. It is fortunate nobody outside the fight was hurt."
One witness said she and her daughter had just boarded the train and sat down when they heard multiple shots being fired on the platform.
"All of a sudden I heard a shot, and then there was like a mass exodus. Everyone started running out, and then there was at least probably three more [shots]," the daughter said.
The MTA says due to the NYPD investigation, C, D and E trains are bypassing Seventh Avenue station in both directions, and E trains are running on the F line from West Fourth Street-Washington Square to 47th-50th Streets-Rockefeller Center.
There are delays in both directions on the A, C, D, E and F lines, the MTA says.
Stay with CBS News New York for the latest on this developing story.

Shooting at NYC subway station leaves man critically injured
A 34-year-old man was critically injured in a shooting aboard a northbound E train in Manhattan, disrupting subway services.
A man was critically injured after being shot aboard a northbound E train at the Seventh Avenue and 53rd Street subway station in Manhattan, New York City, on Saturday, October 17, 2026, according to the New York Police Department (NYPD). Emergency medical services took the victim to a hospital, where he was in critical condition.
The shooting was reported at around 12:21 p.m. after a 911 call, according to FOX 5 New York. Police have not released the man's name or age. Authorities have also not confirmed what led to the gunfire or publicly identified a suspect in the reports available so far. The investigation is ongoing.
34-year-old man shot at 53rd Street subway station
The New York Post reported that the victim was 34 years old and had been shot in the chest. According to the newspaper, two male suspects fired shots from inside the northbound E train towards the platform.
The man received CPR on the platform before being taken to Bellevue Hospital in cardiac arrest, the New York Post reported, citing police sources. FOX 5 New York also confirmed that the victim was in critical condition.
Police have not released the victim’s identity. Authorities have also not confirmed whether anyone has been arrested or provided a description of the suspected shooters. The reason for the shooting has not been established.

E, C and D subway trains face service changes
The shooting also affected subway services in Manhattan. According to the Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA), uptown E trains were running via the F line between West Fourth Street and Jackson Heights-Roosevelt Avenue. Uptown C and D trains were bypassing the Seventh Avenue station.
The changes affected passengers travelling through the area following the shooting. The available reports did not confirm when normal service would resume.
Police are continuing to investigate the incident. Further details about the suspects, the events leading up to the shooting and the victim’s condition have not been confirmed in the latest reports reviewed.

sources.text:
MIDTOWN, Manhattan (WABC) -- A man died after being shot on a northbound E train platform at the Seventh Avenue-53rd Street subway station on Saturday, according to police.
It happened shortly before 12:30 p.m. Sources said the victim and the suspect were arguing on the platform before the shooting. The dispute then spilled onto the train and back onto the platform.
Police say they are still investigating whether shots were fired on the platform or on the train.
The victim was transported to Bellevue Hospital in critical condition, where police later confirmed he died. His identity has not been released, but he is said to be in his thirties.
A woman who identified herself as Miller tells Eyewitness News that her daughter came face to face with the gunman.
"We heard five rounds and my daughter said 'omg there's the shooter,'" she said.
The incident disrupted subway service. According to the MTA, uptown E trains were running via the F line from West Fourth Street to Jackson Heights-Roosevelt Avenue. Uptown C and D trains were bypassing Seventh Avenue.
No arrests have been announced, and the investigation remains ongoing. The suspect was last seen traveling northbound on 7th Avenue. He was wearing a red tracksuit, a black vest and a black face mask and carrying a backpack. Police have not recovered a weapon.
Police say the shooting was not a random act.
MTA Chief Security Officer Michael Kemper released a statement Saturday saying,
"Guns have no place in transit which is why we've strongly supported New York State's legal fight to make sure it's illegal to carry them in the subway system. This was evidently a dispute between two individuals that ended tragically, and we have coordinated with the NYPD on the investigation from the earliest minutes -- especially to retrieve video from platform and train car cameras. The perpetrator will be caught and should face maximum consequences from the justice system. It is fortunate nobody outside the fight was hurt."

sources.news_title: Man shot and killed inside Midtown subway station
sources.text:
Man shot and killed inside Midtown subway station
See more of our coverage in your search results.
A man was shot and killed after an argument in a Midtown subway station Saturday afternoon turned deadly, police and sources said.
The gunfire erupted inside the 7th Avenue station at 53rd Street, located in tourist-packed Midtown West, at 12:21 p.m., the NYPD said.
First responders administered CPR on the platform before rushing the man to Bellevue Hospital in cardiac arrest, where he was pronounced dead, sources said.
He, the gunman and another individual had engaged in some type of dispute on the northbound platform, though the details are not yet clear, according to NYPD Deputy Chief Keith Shine.
Police have yet to recover a weapon and the NYPD warned that the suspect on the loose is armed and dangerous.
It’s also not clear whether the gunman knew the victim, but police emphasized the shooting was targeted.
“Nothing random between these two individuals,” an NYPD spokesperson told The Post at the scene.
An E train had pulled up to the platform and opened its doors just moments before the shooting occurred, with one witness telling The Post he heard two “pops” roughly eight seconds apart, sending straphangers into a frenzy.
“Everybody was running,” said Mauricio Marroquin, who was on his way home to Queens after working a morning shift as a breakfast attendant.
“I seen a gentleman laying right in front,” Marroquin said of the victim. “He was dressed in a blazer, looked like he was coming from work or something, bro. Going to work or coming from work. It was two shots, man. He only got hit with one, like, that’s weird. And they were eight seconds apart, man. That’s weird.”
Marroquin said several bystanders surrounded the victim, one of whom began chest compressions until EMS arrived and another who held the injured man’s hand.
“Another gentleman was just talking to him, like, ‘Hey, man, wake up, wake up, stay up, stay up, stay up,'” said Marroquin.
Harrowing video obtained by The Post shows first responders frantically doing chest compressions on the victim as he lay on the ground of the crowded platform.
Police are searching for the suspect, who was last seen wearing a red tracksuit, black puffer vest and what appeared to be a black balaclava, security footage shows.
The shooting marks the seventh murder in the New York City transit system so far this year.
Transit murders are up 75% compared to the same period last year, which saw just four, according to data through Sunday.
“Guns have no place in transit, which is why we’ve strongly supported New York State’s legal fight to make sure it’s illegal to carry them in the subway system,” Michael Kemper, MTA’s Chief Security Officer, said in a statement.
He added that the MTA has been coordinating with the NYPD, and that the perps in this shooting will be tracked down and “should face maximum consequences from the justice system.”
But commuters who spoke with The Post weren’t buying promises of subway safety.
“To be honest I’m not really sure how effective it’s been. I hear a lot of talk. So, I don’t know if there is actual action behind it,” said lifelong New Yorker Leslie, 50, a housekeeper from the Bronx.
“I don’t feel safe in the city, and I absolutely don’t feel safe on the train at all. Not even a little bit.”
“Are they going to have to, like, put in metal detectors in the subway now?” lamented Priscilla Rodriguez, 35, a data analyst from Rhode Island who was in Midtown visiting her sister.
“I just think it’s sad people can’t live their lives, their daily lives, go on about their business without being unsafe.”

The New York Police Department (NYPD) said they are searching for the suspect.
Police said the shooting was reported shortly before 12:21 p.m. on the northbound E train platform at the 53rd Street-Seventh Avenue station in Manhattan near Times Square.
Investigators said an unidentified man approached another unidentified man, displayed a gun, and fired once, hitting him in the chest.
First responders tried to save the man's life at the scene before he was taken to NYC Health + Hospitals/Bellevue, where he was pronounced dead, police said.
Police did not release a possible motive or say whether the men knew each other. They also didn't say what led up to the dispute.
The suspect ran from the station and was last seen heading north on Seventh Avenue, police said. He was described as a man wearing a red tracksuit, black vest and black face mask, and carrying a backpack.
The killing occurred in the Midtown North Precinct and Transit District 1, an area that includes some of the city's busiest subway stations and tourist corridors.
Police asked anyone with information about the suspect to contact Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS. Tips can also be submitted online through the Crime Stoppers website or through the NYPD Tips account on X.
The investigation is still ongoing, police said.

sources.text:
Man fatally shot after dispute on Manhattan subway platform
Police found an adult man suffering from a gunshot wound to the chest on the E train platform, according to a police spokesperson.
A man was shot and killed Saturday afternoon following a dispute on a subway platform in Midtown Manhattan, prompting service disruptions as police investigated.
The shooting occurred around 12:20 p.m. at the Seventh Avenue and West 53rd Street station, near Broadway theaters and Carnegie Hall.
Police found an adult man suffering from a gunshot wound to the chest on the E train platform, according to a police spokesperson. The shooting followed an altercation involving two or three men.
Emergency responders transported the victim to Bellevue Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
No arrests had been reported immediately following the shooting, and authorities continued investigating the circumstances surrounding the deadly confrontation.
Subway trains that normally serve the station bypassed the area while police worked at the scene, disrupting service for commuters traveling through Midtown.

sources.text:

"This was evidently a dispute between two individuals that ended tragically, and we have coordinated with the NYPD on the investigation from the earliest minutes -- especially to retrieve video from platform and train car cameras," MTA Chief Security Officer Michael Kemper said in a statement. Police confirmed later at a news conference that they do not believe the killing was a random act.
The man died at Bellevue Hospital.
"My daughter said, 'Oh my God, there's a shooter!' And so people started hovering together, hovering, and she walked out," a tourist who identified herself as "Miller" told reporters at the scene. NEW YORK - A man is dead after being shot on a subway platform in Manhattan on Saturday afternoon.
Officers responded to a 911 call around 12:21 p.m. reporting a shooting on a subway platform at the 53rd Street and 7th Avenue station.
What we know:
Emergency medical services responded to the scene and transported the victim to a local area hospital where he was pronounced dead.
Authorities have not released the identity or age of the victim.

What they're saying:
In a statement Saturday, MTA Chief Security Officer Michael Kemper said that the shooting was apparently the result of a dispute between two men, and said that the MTA is working with the NYPD to find more footage of the time surrounding the shooting, with the hopes of catching the suspected shooter.

sources.news_title: Man Fatally Shot Inside Midtown Manhattan Subway Station, NYPD Says
sources.text:
A man was fatally shot inside a New York City subway station Saturday afternoon, the NYPD confirmed to News Media.
The gunfire erupted shortly after noon at the 53rd Street and Seventh Avenue station in crowded Midtown Manhattan, according to police.
Hassen Pinchback, who was visiting from Orlando, Florida, told News Media that passengers began fleeing as soon as they heard the shots.
“It was like a stampede,” he said.
Pinchback said the shooting began when the train doors opened. “That’s when you heard pop pop pop,” he recalled. A female bystander was performing chest compressions on the wounded man before officers arrived, urging him to “Hang in there.”
Another witness from Washington state, who identified herself only by the last name Miller, said she and her daughter heard roughly five shots while seated in a subway car with its doors open. Her daughter stepped outside, and Miller said the gunman looked directly at her before continuing to fire.
“I just started praying. I’m a very strong Christian,” she said. “Jesus saved us. 100%.”
Miller said her daughter signaled a conductor aboard another train to warn him about the shooter. The conductor then called 911.
The victim was taken to a hospital in critical condition, where he later succumbed to his injuries.
The NYPD said the investigation remains active and no arrests have been announced.
PIX11 reported that the shooting followed an argument between the victim and the gunman.
